name: @w6w-apps/jenkins
description: Trigger builds, inspect jobs, and manage the build queue on any Jenkins instance.

w6w.longDescription:
Jenkins connects a workflow to any Jenkins instance — a customer's own CI box, an on-prem network segment, or a managed offering — to trigger builds, inspect jobs, manage the build queue and stop a build in progress. Because Jenkins is almost always self-hosted, the instance's own base URL is collected on the connection rather than pinned to a single vendor host, and every action builds its request against that URL.

Triggering a build queues it rather than starting it immediately; the useful part of the response is a queue item, which a separate action resolves once Jenkins actually schedules an executor and hands back the real build number. Job names accept a folder path, so builds inside a Folders-plugin or multibranch-pipeline layout are addressed the same way a flat job would be.

Authentication is HTTP Basic with a username and personal API token — the credential form Jenkins itself documents as CSRF-exempt, so no separate crumb needs to be fetched or attached to any write.
